## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical design for per-tenant feature gating in CNF gateways, including secure identity, dynamic policy delivery, and runtime enforcement. It emphasizes end-to-end testability and real-world trade-offs between performance and isolation.

## Key Concepts

- per-tenant policy CRD
- bidirectional gRPC capability negotiation
- in-memory enforcement with cache invalidation
- SPIFFE/SVID-based mutual TLS for control plane–sidecar trust
- canary-friendly rollout and end-to-end validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal CRD blueprint (high level)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: cnffeaturepolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                tenantID:
                  type: string
                features:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: cnffeaturepolicies
    singular: cnffeaturepolicy
    kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
    shortNames: [cfp]
```

```yaml
# Sample policy (per-tenant)
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-policy
spec:
  tenantID: tenant-a
  features:
    - QUIC
    - TLS13
    - multiplexing
```

```yaml
# Minimal end-to-end test manifest (one namespace)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: mycnf/gateway:latest
          args: ["--config", "/etc/gateway/config.yaml"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/gateway
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: gateway-config
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates your ability to design end-to-end provenance controls for CNF environments, specifically addressing how key rotation impacts SBOM generation and policy enforcement in multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign image signing with KMS-backed keys
- SPDX SBOM generation and attestation workflows
- Kyverno policy enforcement for signature and SBOM validation
- Key rotation impact on image provenance chains
- Namespace-scoped testing strategies and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```bash
# Sign image with KMS-backed key
cosign sign --key kms://mykms/path/to/key \
  --attachment sbom \
  registry.example.com/cnf:latest

# Generate and attach SBOM
syft registry.example.com/cnf:latest \
  -o spdx-json > sbom.spdx

cosign attest --key kms://mykms/path/to/key \
  --type spdx --predicate sbom.spdx \
  registry.example.com/cnf:latest
```

## Implementation Strategy
Deploy this solution progressively: start with image signing, add SBOM generation, implement Kyverno policies, then automate the key rotation workflow. Test in isolated namespaces before cluster-wide deployment.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses the ability to design per-tenant feature flag canary deployments in Cloud-Native Functions (CNFs), including CRD-driven configuration, deterministic traffic steering, rollback mechanisms, and observability considerations.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant feature flags via custom Kubernetes CRD
- Deterministic routing using HMAC hashing for consistent tenant-to-canary assignment
- Canary rollout semantics with percentage-based traffic splitting
- Rollback strategies and observability per tenant

## Solution Overview
The solution uses a TenantFlags CRD to define per-tenant feature flag configurations. The sidecar gateway computes HMAC-SHA256(tenantID + flag) to derive a hash value between 0-99. If this value is less than the rolloutPct, traffic routes to canaryPath; otherwise, it uses baselinePath.

### TenantFlags CRD
```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantFlags
metadata:
  name: tenant-flags
  namespace: cnf-gateway
spec:
  tenants:
    - tenantId: "tenant-001"
      flags:
        - name: "new-payment-api"
          canaryPath: "/api/v2/payments"
          baselinePath: "/api/v1/payments"
          rolloutPct: 15
        - name: "enhanced-search"
          canaryPath: "/search/v2"
          baselinePath: "/search/v1"
          rolloutPct: 10
```

### Example Tenant Configuration
```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantFlags
metadata:
  name: acme-corp-flags
  namespace: cnf-gateway
spec:
  tenants:
    - tenantId: "acme-corp"
      flags:
        - name: "graphql-schema"
          canaryPath: "/graphql/v2"
          baselinePath: "/graphql/v1"
          rolloutPct: 25
```

### One-Namespace Validation Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
---
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenantflags.cnf.example
spec:
  group: cnf.example
  names:
    kind: TenantFlags
    plural: tenantflags
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
```

- **Immediate Rollback**: Set rolloutPct to 0 to instantly redirect all traffic to baseline

- **Tracing**: Propagate tenant context through distributed traces to identify canary traffic patterns
- **Alerts**: Monitor error rates and latency differences between canary and baseline paths per tenant
- **Dashboards**: Visualize rollout progress and health metrics for each tenant's feature flags

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: cnf-provenance-policy

  rules:
  - name: verify-image-signature

      any:
      - resources:

```

```yaml
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a

  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  template:
    spec:

      - name: cnf-gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:latest
        env:
        - name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT

            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.trace
              key: cnf.trace.target
      - name: otel-collector

        args: ["--config=/etc/otel/config.yaml"]

          mountPath: /etc/otel
      volumes:

        configMap:
          name: otel-collector-config
```

## Adaptive Sampling Implementation
```go
func AdaptiveSampler(sampleRate float64, errorRate float64) float64 {
    baseRate := sampleRate
    if errorRate > 0.05 {
        return min(1.0, baseRate*2)
    }
    return baseRate
}
```

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 5
      - pause: {duration: 5m}
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: error-rate-check
        successfulRunHistoryLimit: 3
        failedRunHistoryLimit: 3
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests real-world per-tenant canary strategies, traffic splitting, and rollback logic under latency and error constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Canary rollout with per-tenant isolation
- Prometheus metric-driven analysis
- Rollout/VirtualService integration
- Safe rollback and promotion windows

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-rollout
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: ghcr.io/org/gateway:canary
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 900s }
      - setWeight: 100
```

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  http:
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: gateway
        subset: stable
      weight: 90
    - destination:
        host: gateway
        subset: canary
      weight: 10
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you map per-tenant metrics to the analysis step to avoid cross-tenant bleed?
- How would you handle multi-namespace rollouts with shared control plane?
